description: Wire the real brand logo into the header via the existing BrandMark.astro asset path, reconcile the placeholders checklist and the one test that pins the wordmark-only state, and remove the excessive empty space below the header. No component rewrite: the swap-in is settings + the smallest CSS/data change. Preserve the logo artwork exactly; preserve header design, navigation, animations, and responsive behavior otherwise.
steps: Enable the asset in data/site/settings.json: set logo.src to '/brand/new-galaxy-furniture-logo.jpeg' (a public/ file is served at its path minus 'public/'), and set logo.width and logo.height to the asset's intrinsic pixel dimensions (currently 1254 and 1254). The schema (src/schemas/site.ts) superRefine makes width AND height REQUIRED as soon as src is non-null, so both must be present or the content gate/build fails. Keep logo.wordmarkFallback unchanged.

Remove 'site.logo.src' from the settings.placeholders array in data/site/settings.json, because the logo is now real. This matches recomputePlaceholders() in src/lib/site/store.ts, which drops that key once logo.src is non-null, and keeps getPlaceholderKeys()/the admin content checklist truthful.

Reconcile tests/unit/homepage.contracts.test.ts: the test titled 'tracks the unsupplied hero image and logo, so the hero is a swap and not a redraw' asserts settings.placeholders.toContain('site.logo.src') and settings.logo.src.toBeNull(). The logo is now supplied, so update this test so it still guards the intended invariant: the hero image is still an unsupplied placeholder (keep the 'site.heroImage' assertion), and the logo is now a real asset (assert settings.logo.src is the '/brand/new-galaxy-furniture-logo.jpeg' path, that settings.logo.width and settings.logo.height are positive integers, and that 'site.logo.src' is NOT in settings.placeholders). Do not weaken the heroImage assertion. Only change what the settings change actually invalidates.

Diagnose the ACTUAL source of the excessive empty space below the header against the built output and the header/brand CSS in src/styles/shell.css and src/components/ui/BrandMark.astro. Candidates: the .ngf-brand column layout (display:inline-flex; flex-direction:column; gap:0.375rem), the wordmark-only champagne hairline (.ngf-brand[data-brand-source='wordmark']::after with height 1px + margin-top 0.375rem), the @media(max-width:767px) .ngf-brand { min-height:44px } touch-target rule, and header padding (.ngf-header{padding:0.75rem 1rem 0}, .ngf-header-inner{padding:0.5rem 0.75rem}). Note that swapping to the asset already removes the wordmark hairline automatically. Apply the SMALLEST correct change that removes the excess vertical space while: keeping the >=44px touch target on mobile (Requirement 24.3), preserving aspect ratio, not stretching, and not altering the header design/nav/animations. Do not restyle beyond the spacing fix.

Optional and only if genuinely justified for correct header sizing: trim the surrounding EMPTY background of public/brand/new-galaxy-furniture-logo.jpeg so the 32px-tall header mark is not dominated by margin. If you trim, trim ONLY whitespace (alter no artwork), keep it the same asset (not a redesign), preserve aspect ratio, overwrite the same file path, and update logo.width/height in settings.json to the trimmed file's REAL new dimensions (read them off the trimmed file, do not guess). Document exactly what you did, the tool used, and the before/after dimensions in findings. If trimming is not warranted, leave the file untouched and say so in findings.
Run `npm run check` and fix any type/astro errors introduced.

Run `npm run build` and confirm all 7 postbuild audits pass, especially scripts/audit-image-loading.ts. If audit-image-loading reports the logo (e.g. 'no reserved box', 'no intrinsic width/height', or a loading/decoding complaint), fix it with the smallest correct change rather than disabling the audit. Confirm the logo in dist/client carries width+height, loading='lazy', decoding='async', alt='New Galaxy Furniture', and is wrapped in .
Run `npm test` (vitest run) and confirm the reconciled homepage.contracts test passes and no NEW unrelated failures appear versus the FEAT-001 baseline.

Verify responsiveness by inspecting the built CSS and the .ngf-brand-asset rules (heights sm 24px / md 32px header / lg 56px, width:auto so aspect ratio is preserved) and by reasoning about behavior at 320, 375, 390, 414, 768, 1024, 1280 px. Confirm no rule would force horizontal overflow of the header row. Record clearly in findings what was verified via build/DOM/CSS inspection vs. what still needs a human eyeball in a real browser.
acceptance_criteria: data/site/settings.json has logo.src='/brand/new-galaxy-furniture-logo.jpeg' with logo.width and logo.height set to the asset's real intrinsic dimensions, and 'site.logo.src' removed from placeholders.

`npm run build` passes all 7 postbuild audits, and dist/client contains the logo with intrinsic width+height, loading='lazy', decoding='async', alt='New Galaxy Furniture', wrapped in a homepage link .
`npm test` passes the reconciled tests/unit/homepage.contracts.test.ts with no new unrelated failures.
The excessive empty space below the header is removed via the smallest correct CSS change, with the >=44px mobile touch target preserved and the header design/nav/animations otherwise unchanged.
The logo artwork is preserved exactly (either untouched, or only whitespace-trimmed with aspect ratio kept and intrinsic dimensions updated to match).

findings documents the spacing diagnosis, the exact change made, whether the asset was trimmed (and before/after dimensions if so), and the responsive verification boundary (CSS/DOM vs. human eyeball).
verification: `npm run build` => all 7 postbuild audits pass; grep dist/client for the logo and confirm src, width, height, alt, loading, decoding, and the enclosing .
`npx vitest run tests/unit/homepage.contracts.test.ts` passes; `npm test` shows no new unrelated failures.

Inspect the built CSS for .ngf-brand-asset and header/brand rules to confirm aspect ratio is preserved (width:auto), the excess space is gone, and no rule forces horizontal overflow at the target widths.
findings: IMPLEMENTED and verified. No wrangler dev was running (checked node/workerd processes: none), so the FEAT-001 EPERM dist\client lock did not recur; both builds completed cleanly. EXACT EDITS (4 files, all in-scope): 1) data/site/settings.json: logo.src set from null to '/brand/new-galaxy-furniture-logo.jpeg'; added logo.width and logo.height (schema superRefine requires both once src is non-null). Values set to the TRIMMED asset's REAL measured dimensions 736 x 918 (see trim note). logo.wordmarkFallback left unchanged. Removed 'site.logo.src' from the placeholders array (it was the first entry) so the committed file matches recomputePlaceholders() in src/lib/site/store.ts, which drops that key once logo.src is non-null; 'site.heroImage' and all other placeholders kept. 2) tests/unit/homepage.contracts.test.ts: reconciled the test 'tracks the unsupplied hero image and logo...' (renamed to '...the now-supplied logo...'). It no longer asserts placeholders contains 'site.logo.src' or that logo.src is null. It now keeps the 'site.heroImage' placeholder assertion (NOT weakened), and asserts settings.logo.src === '/brand/new-galaxy-furniture-logo.jpeg', that logo.width and logo.height are positive integers, and that 'site.logo.src' is NOT in placeholders. Only what the settings change invalidated was changed. 3) src/components/ui/BrandMark.astro (CSS only, no markup/component rewrite): scoped the .ngf-brand column 'gap: 0.375rem' to '.ngf-brand[data-brand-source="wordmark"]' only, so the supplied asset (a single flex child) carries no vestigial column gap. Everything else (flex-direction:column, the mobile min-height:44px touch target, the wordmark hairline ::after, the .ngf-brand-asset height rules sm 24/md 32/lg 56 with width:auto) is unchanged. 4) public/brand/new-galaxy-furniture-logo.jpeg: whitespace-trimmed (see below). SPACING DIAGNOSIS: The header is position:sticky top:0 so it stays in flow and does not overlay a gap; the section band paddings in index.astro (clamp(3rem,8vh,6rem)) are the intended design rhythm and were left untouched. Against the built output/CSS the actual source of the 'excessive empty space' around the header mark was the ASSET itself: the real file was 1254x1254 square with a large empty cream margin (measured content bounding box was 288,240 -> 976,1110, i.e. 688x870 of artwork inside ~280px side / 240px top / 144px bottom of empty background). Rendered at height:32px width:auto that square, mostly-empty image produced a ~32x32 box whose visible mark was only ~22px and which was dominated by baked-in margin. The secondary contributor was the .ngf-brand column 'gap' inherited into asset mode (harmless as a single-child gap, but dead intent). The wordmark champagne hairline is auto-removed by the asset (data-brand-source flips to 'asset'), confirmed in built CSS (the ::after is scoped to [data-brand-source=wordmark]). Smallest correct fix: trim ONLY the empty background of the asset (removes the dominating margin) and scope the column gap to wordmark mode. The >=44px mobile touch target (.ngf-brand min-height:44px) was preserved; header/nav/animations untouched. ASSET TRIM: YES, trimmed. Tool: PowerShell System.Drawing (GDI+). Method: sampled the cream background from a corner (RGB 252,242,232), scanned all pixels with a per-channel tolerance of 28 to find the artwork bounding box (288,240 -> 976,1110), then cropped to that box PLUS a uniform 24px breathing-room margin on all sides (final crop rect x0=264 y0=216 w=736 h=918), re-encoded JPEG at quality 90, and overwrote the same path. NO artwork was altered, recolored, redrawn, or cropped into: only surrounding empty cream background was removed. BEFORE: 1254x1254 px, 54477 bytes, square. AFTER: 736x918 px, 61681 bytes (slightly larger bytes because the frame is now denser detail with less flat background). Aspect ratio is that of the artwork itself (portrait ~0.802:1); rendered at height:32px it is ~25.7px wide. Visual check of the trimmed file confirmed the full lockup is intact (NG monogram + pendant lamp + chair inside the gold circle, and the 'NEW GALAXY FURNITURE / FURNITURE / Modern & Minimalist' wordmark). settings.logo.width/height were set to the trimmed file's REAL measured dimensions (736/918), read off the file, not guessed. audit-image-loading SUMMARY LINE after the change (npm run build, both builds identical): '[image-loading] 25 page(s), 67 image(s): 5 prioritised and 5 preloaded, each one paired; every other image lazy and async, every box reserved, no card served at full resolution, search index outside every initial payload.' Image count rose from the 16 pre-logo baseline to 67 because the logo now renders on all 25 pages (plus the hero eyebrow BrandMark size='sm' instance). 'every box reserved' confirms the logo's reserved box holds: the built CSS still contains '.ngf-brand-md .ngf-brand-asset { height:32px }' which registers 'ngf-brand-md' and 'ngf-brand-asset' as box-reserving classes, and the img's ancestor carries 'ngf-brand-md'. The audit did NOT report the logo; no audit was disabled. All 7 postbuild audits pass (motion-budget, emit-redirects, audit-seo, audit-csp, page-budget, image-loading, keyword-density). BUILT-OUTPUT CONFIRMATION (dist/client/index.html): the header brand renders as . Carries intrinsic width+height, lazy+async, correct alt, wrapped in the homepage link. Built CSS confirms gap scoped to wordmark, min-height:44px present, asset heights 24/32/56 with width:auto. RECONCILED-TEST RESULT: npx vitest run tests/unit/homepage.contracts.test.ts => 21/21 PASS. Full npm test => 5 failed | 967 passed (972); the 5 failures are EXACTLY the FEAT-001 pre-existing Windows-only baseline noise (seo.meta.test.ts path separators; security.build-output.test.ts x2 AI_API_KEY scan + real token in local .dev.vars; supporting-pages-showroom.test.ts CRLF; analytics.snapshot.test.ts CRLF). NO new failures introduced. npm run check => 0 errors, 0 warnings, 21 hints (identical to baseline). RESPONSIVE VERIFICATION BOUNDARY: Verified via built CSS/DOM reasoning (NO live browser available per environment_constraints): (a) aspect ratio preserved at every size because .ngf-brand-asset is width:auto with only a fixed height (sm 24px used in footer/mobile bar/hero eyebrow, md 32px in header, lg 56px in hero) — the browser derives width from the intrinsic 736:918, so no stretch; (b) at 320/375/390/414 px the header brand is flex:0 1 auto with min-width:0 inside .ngf-header-inner (flex row, gap 0.5rem) and a ~26px-wide mark cannot force horizontal overflow beside the compact search/enquiry/menu controls; the wordmark-only wrap rule (.ngf-header-brand .ngf-brand-wordmark flex-wrap:wrap) is now inert since the wordmark does not render in asset mode; (c) at 768 px the mobile min-height:44px touch target still applies (media max-width:767px ends at 767, so 768 is desktop-tools breakpoint boundary; touch target guaranteed through 767px inclusive); (d) at 1024/1280 px the desktop nav+tools show and the ~26px mark sits left with margin-right:auto, no overflow. WHAT NEEDS A HUMAN EYEBALL in a real browser: the subjective visual balance of the trimmed mark at 32px in the live header (whether the tiny wordmark text under the monogram reads acceptably at header scale is a design judgment, not a layout bug), the transparent-over-hero vs scrolled states, and confirming there is no perceptible vertical gap under the sticky header on an actual device. NOT COMMITTED per user requirement.
